source.title: Normalized Flat Minima: Exploring Scale Invariant Definition of Flat Minima for Neural Networks using PAC-Bayesian Analysis
source.authors: Yusuke Tsuzuku; Issei Sato; Masashi Sugiyama

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether normalized sharpness tracks generalization gap using a scale-aware measure, and compares it with existing sharpness metrics.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a qualitative relationship between sharpness measures and accuracy gap in figures and describes that relationship in the text. It does not report numerical gap or sharpness values by model and random-label ratio. The cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests whether a magnitude-aware, scale-invariant sharpness measure tracks train–test accuracy gaps, using a different measure and random-label mixtures. This bears on V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose a flatness definition invariant to the discussed rescalings and report that it distinguishes overfitted models better than existing measures, including in larger networks. Their empirical conclusions are suggestive, not a universal or causal guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a PAC-Bayesian normalized sharpness measure and compares it with Hessian trace and squared Frobenius norms; it does not reproduce the version's cited study or full protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior depends on the sharpness measure: normalized sharpness gives a stronger signal than unnormalized measures, which lose distinguishing ability for larger models with normalization layers.
record.problems: Results are mainly qualitative scatter plots without numerical per-model values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use random-label mixtures and MNIST/CIFAR-10 only; no SVHN experiment is reported. The authors note that the positive-semidefinite assumption for the Hessian may be false.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label training fit is stated, but held-out natural-label and random-label accuracies, including a chance-level random-label control, are not separately established.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
Adam is used without an optimizer comparison.

No SVHN experiment, full norm-and-margin comparison suite, or direct reproduction of the original perturbation-tolerance measure. Near-perfect training accuracy is established, but similarly low training loss is not documented. The experiments vary label corruption rather than the original study's broader training choices.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

missing.what: Numerical correlation comparison for Wide ResNet: Hessian trace 70.8 and normalized sharpness 91.1, as printed. Record these separately and retain the paper's reporting scale.

record.verdict_notes: Weakness of unnormalized comparators supports the motivation for magnitude-aware sharpness; it does not limit V7. Failure to test the complete comparison suite belongs under untested. All four model–dataset pairs have 100 runs total, with a random-label ratio sampled independently each run, rather than 100 runs per ratio. No external sources were consulted.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains on random-label mixtures but does not report held-out accuracy for natural labels versus random labels, nor chance-level performance on held-out random labels.
No network-width sweep or test-error comparison beyond an interpolation threshold.

No SVHN results; no comparison across networks explicitly matched for similarly low training loss; the study tests random-label ratios on MNIST and CIFAR-10. It compares normalized sharpness with trace of the Hessian and squared Frobenius norms, not the full set of norm- and margin-based measures named in the version.
